entries.bestHook: 'Two people born weeks apart can share a star sign and still have almost nothing else in common on the chart.' Editorial pick backed by the thin reach signal: the sharpest statement of the whole-chart differentiator and the furthest-traveled post of the week.

Until posts reach people, no hook or CTA test can produce signal.

Ranked on raw reach as the distribution proxy (method B1: while reach is the binding constraint, read distribution, not hooks or CTAs). entries.clicksToFreeChart: No measurable signal. Facebook post link clicks = 0 across all posts (reach too low for clicks regardless); the Oct 29 FB Reel carried the UTM chart link in-caption and recorded 0 link clicks on reach 0. Instagram stays link-in-bio, no per-post click data.
entries.bestHook: Oct 29 Moon-in-Cancer Reel: 'What makes a place feel like home to you?' Furthest-traveled item of the week. In plain terms it names a feeling everyone recognises and invites a one-word answer, and it rode the Reel format that actually reaches non-followers. Runner-up on structure: the pillar 'Ever read your horoscope and felt it was written for a stranger?', which opens on the reader's own experience (problem first) before any astrology. Both are editorial reads: reach is still too thin to crown a hook.
entries.weakestHook: The today's-sky posts that open on planetary mechanics before any human angle, e.g. Oct 25 'With Venus moving backward through the sky, today's meeting with the Sun has a reflective, looking-back quality.' A cold reader has no reason to care by line one; the relatable question is buried under the jargon. Lowest views-per-reach of the week. Caveat: single-digit reach makes this a read, not a verdict.
entries.oneChange: Format, for Monday 2026-11-02: make the 18:00 pillar slot a Reel/video too, so both Monday slots are video rather than one Reel plus one static image. The week's single Reel reached 9 vs 1-5 for every static feed post, and on a roughly 5-follower account Reels are the one format Instagram shows to non-followers. Reach is the binding constraint in launch (method B1), so move the static pillars toward video before testing hooks or CTAs.
entries.crossBrandLesson: First hard number behind the already-recorded launch-weeks rule (B1): on a near-empty account a single Reel reached 9 people vs 1-5 for static feed posts. Genuinely cross-brand but n=1 so far; proposed as the first B2 'Content that works' data point once a second week confirms it. No method change needed this week.

entries.ranking: Could not rank by (saves+shares)/reach: saves and shares are zero on every post this week, so the ratio is zero across the board. Fell back to reach. Clear pattern: Reels far outreach static feed images. On Instagram, the 6 today's-sky Reels reached ~160 people combined (best: Nov 5 Reel, reach 72, views 85) versus ~17 total for the 6 static pillar feed posts. Facebook reach stayed at 0-1 per post on both formats.
entries.clicksToFreeChart: No signal yet. Facebook in-post link clicks = 0 all week (the full chart URL + UTM is now in FB post text, per last week's change, so the pipe is in place; reach is the bottleneck, not the CTA). Instagram remains link-in-bio and exposes no per-post click metric.
entries.bestHook: Instagram, Oct 31 pillar: 'Heard people mention their big three and nodded along without being quite sure what it meant?' Top feed reach (5) and views (7) and one of only two likes all week. Why it works: it names a phrase people have actually heard in conversation (the big three) and admits the small discomfort of not knowing it, which is a precise, personal curiosity gap rather than a generic question.
entries.weakestHook: Instagram, Nov 5 pillar: 'Ever read your horoscope and feel it could belong to anyone?' Bottom of the week on reach (1) and views (1). Why it is weak: an abstract yes/no rhetorical opener built on a familiar cliche; it does not name anything concrete or promise a specific payoff, so it gives a cold scroller no reason to stop. (The Nov 3 privacy post is also a soft opener, but that is a trust message by design, not a hook.)
entries.oneChange: Format change for Monday's batch: convert the pillar/educational concepts into short Reels (or add at least one Reel-pillar), instead of running them only as static feed images. Reason: on a 3-week-old account with ~5 followers, Reels are the only format reaching non-followers. This week Instagram Reels reached ~160 people versus ~17 for static pillar images, roughly a 9x gap. The pillar writing is strong; it just needs the format that the algorithm actually distributes to a cold audience. Keep the today's-sky Reels as they are.
